texts.preamble: Rsh Agro Products Limited vs The Union Of India And 2 Ors on 14 October, 2020 Author: Suman Shyam Bench: Suman Shyam Page No.# 1/2 Gahc010144392020 The Gauhati High Court (High Court Of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram And Arunachal Pradesh) Case No. : Wp(C) 4316/2020 1:Rsh Agro Products Limited Cin No. U15132As2021Plc012193, Represented By Its Chief Financial Officer- Sri Pramod Kumar Choudhury, Having Its Registered Office At- Village Ambher, 12Th Mile, Jorabat, Guwahati-781023, Kamrup(M), Assam Versus 1:The Union Of India And 2 Ors. Represented By The Secretary, Ministry Of Health And Family Welfare, Government Of India, Food Regulation Section, Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi-110011 2:Food Safety And Standards Authority Of India ( A Statutory Authority Established Under The Food Safety And Standards Act 2006 India) Represented By Its Authorized Representative/Advisor Fda Bhawan Kolta Road New Delhi-110002 3:Commissioner Of Food Safety Health And Family Welfare Department Assam Secretariat Block-D 4Th Floor Dispur-781006 Assam Advocate for the Petitioner : Mr D K Das Rsh Agro Products Limited vs The Union Of India And 2 Ors on 14 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195517003/ 1 Advocate for the Respondent : Asstt.S.G.I. Page No.# Before Honourable Mr. Justice Suman Shyam Order 14.10.2020
texts.facts: Since the notification has already been stayed, hence, there cannot be any impediment on the part of the petitioner to operate the unit. However, despite stay of the impugned notification, Mr. Agarwala submits that the authorities have asked each unit to obtain separate orders from the Court so as to resume operation.
texts.arguments: Petitioners are aggrieved by the notification dated 23-09-2020, whereby prohibition on blending of edible vegetable oil with the mustered oil has been imposed w.e.f. 01-10- 2020. Mr. Agarwala, learned counsel submits that such order of prohibition could not have been issued by the authorities in violation of Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 more so, when the draft amendment to the regulation has yet to receive the approval of the parliament. The learned counsel has also invited the attention of this Court to the interim order dated 29-09-2020 passed by the Delhi High Court in ( B.R. Oil Industries Pvt. Ltd Vs. Union of India & Anr. ) staying operation of the notification dated 23-09-2020 so as to contend that keeping in mind uniformity in the matter of judicial orders, a similar interim order is required to be passed in this case as well. Mr. Pracha, on the other hand, has refuted the submission made by the learned counsel Page No.# 3/4 for the petitioners to contend that the Central Government is not only authorized to issue appropriate instruction to the Food Authority but in the present case, such instructions have been issued keeping in mind the public interest at large insofar as the food safety measures are concerned. It is also the submission of Mr. Pracha that the interim order dated 29-09-2020 passed by the Delhi High Court was an ex-parte order and the matter is fixed for reconsideration on 22-10-2020. Mr. Agarwala has, however, submitted that there are number of writ petitions pending on the issue before the Delhi High Court and the interim order passed on 29-09-2020 has already been extended by a subsequent order.
